topic: sandbase-harness: Local-First Agent Runtime with Sandboxed Sessions

key_points: Open-source (Apache-2.0) local-first agent runtime: sessions, sandboxed tools, memory, credentials, audit trails, local Console — all on your machine or your own infrastructure
Current traction ~581-647 stars, ~55-69 forks; created 2026-07-11; active commits (110+ from liyangbing)
Sandbox backends: local process, Docker (per-session containers), Kubernetes (kubectl exec/cp), self-hosted worker queue
SQLite-backed agents/sessions/environments/credential vaults/memory/files; resumable Server-Sent Events for session replay; Claude Managed Agents-style /v1 API
Runs any model: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible incl. DeepSeek V4; MCP toolset integration; permission policies and approvals
Ships as a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin bundle over stdio MCP
Local-first terminal agent runtime with isolated subtasks and intent-aware Guard (safety)
Main agent delegates to isolated subtasks with per-subtask tool whitelist, explicit model, explicit context — instead of one giant shared context
JSON-RPC daemon over local/TCP for reuse by Web UIs, IDEs, desktop apps, or scripts
Lightweight profile memory near latest user input; memory, Skills, MCP under user control
PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 license (noncommercial only); ~18 stars, small scale
Boundaries: no full OS sandbox, limited MCP support, no full history search/vector memory yet
Local-first AI desktop assistant — 'Log is the Runtime': model messages, tool calls, results are recorded as recoverable execution facts
Sessions/UI/model context/recovery are projections over a runtime event log; Tool Result pruning and LLM compaction manage context
TaskRuns outlive turns: durable headless work with budgets and continuation/recovery
Surfaces: Electron desktop, TUI/CLI, non-interactive CLI, Headless runner; Apache-2.0
Local tools incl. Read/Write/Edit/Bash; model connections via cloud API, local model, or gateway
The architectural choice (cloud sandbox vs local-first) matters more than benchmarks for enterprise teams

Devin/Cognition = persistent cloud VM per session (source leaves the building); Codex CLI = default local execution + OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt/Landlock/seccomp), optional cloud delegation in ephemeral containers
Local-first advantages: data never leaves perimeter, sub-second feedback loop latency, no per-task cloud billing
Codex CLI workspace-write sandbox: writes only in project dir, network off unless enabled; cloud tasks ephemeral, nothing persists
Regulated industries (finance, healthcare) often require local/on-prem to satisfy residency
MIT-licensed, local-first agent framework; main sessions run with host access restricted to paired-DM contacts, group/channel sessions run in Docker/SSH/OpenShell sandbox
Two-tier execution model separating trusted host sessions from untrusted inbound-channel sessions — a template for sandbox boundaries
Skills materialize under ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/ from ClawHub or local authoring (local-first skill lifecycle)
Used as a canonical case in AI safety research on persistent prompt-injection (Sleeper Channels paper) — motivation for audit trails and sandboxing

stats.fact: Gartner forecasts 40% of enterprise applications will embed task-specific AI agents by end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025.

stats.fact: The agentic AI market was ~USD 7.06B in 2025, projected to reach USD 93.2B by 2032 (44.6% CAGR); the narrower AI agents market is ~USD 7.84B in 2025 growing to USD 52.62B by 2030.
Gartner warns >40% of agentic AI projects risk cancellation by 2027 if governance, observability, and ROI clarity aren't established — driving demand for audit/replay and sandbox controls.
67% of enterprises express concern about AI data privacy, and 42% of EU companies plan on-premise AI deployment by 2027; average data breach cost is $4.44M (IBM 2023).
stats.source: Gartner 2025 / heybeagle.com, Kong Enterprise AI report

stats.fact: By 2028, Gartner projects 33% of enterprise software applications will include agentic AI (up from <1% in 2024) and at least 15% of day-to-day work decisions will be made autonomously by agents.

Enterprise cloud-sandbox vs local-first: local execution yields sub-second feedback-loop latency and keeps source/data inside the org perimeter, critical for regulated (finance/health/defense) workloads.
stats.source: Devin vs Codex CLI comparison, Daniel Vaughan (2026)

angles: Data ownership as the core buying motive — local-first means sessions, credentials, and audit logs never leave your infrastructure; contrast with cloud sandbox VMs
'Production agents need more than a model loop' — persistable sessions, resumable SSE replay, credential vaults, and audit trails are the gap Agent SDKs don't fill
Sandbox depth tiers as a decision framework: local process vs Docker per-session containers vs Kubernetes exec/cp vs self-hosted worker queue, matched to workload trust level
Regulated-industry appeal: finance, healthcare, defense data residency mandates make self-hosted agent runtime the compliance-safe default
Model-agnostic + MCP integration as an anti-lock-in story — bring your own model (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek V4) and existing MCP toolsets
The enterprise governance angle: Gartner's 40%-project-cancellation warning makes audit/replay and permission policies a risk-management purchase, not just a dev-tool nicety
